nodes.summary: The generator of the stochastic mass-action chain restricted to a finite set `Ω` of states: `Q x y = ∑_r λ_r(x) ([fire r x = y] - [x = y])`. It is a rate matrix when `Ω` is closed under firing (`isRateMatrix_classGenerator`).
nodes.title: Generator of the mass-action chain on a finite state class

nodes.summary: Stationary law of the stochastic mass-action chain on a finite class (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1–4.2). Let the rate constants be nonnegative, `c > 0` complex balanced, and `Ω` a nonempty finite set of states closed under the reactions in both directions. Then the restricted generator is a rate matrix, and the normalized product-form Poisson law `π(x) ∝ ∏_s c_s^{x_s} e^{-c_s} / Nat.factorial x_s` on `Ω`…
nodes.title: Stationary law of the stochastic mass-action chain on a finite class

nodes.summary: The Poisson weights normalized on a finite set `Ω` of states.
nodes.title: Normalized Poisson stationary law on a finite state class

nodes.summary: The concentration control coefficient `C^{s_m}_{e_i} = (e_i / s_m) ∂s_m/∂e_i`, meaningful for a positive concentration `s_m` and a steady state differentiable at `e`.
nodes.title: Concentration control coefficient

nodes.summary: Weak duality for flux balance analysis.
nodes.title: Weak duality for flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: The elasticity `ε^{v_i}_{s_m} = (s_m / v_i) ∂v_i/∂s_m`, meaningful for a nonzero rate `v_i` and a rate law differentiable at `s`.
nodes.title: Elasticity of a reaction rate

nodes.summary: For an irreducible rate matrix every invariant vector is a multiple of the in-tree weights: the stationary law is proportional, at each state, to the weight of the spanning in-trees rooted there.
nodes.title: Uniqueness in the Markov chain tree theorem

nodes.summary: Strong duality for flux balance analysis: a feasible problem has a dual feasible point whose value is the optimal value.
nodes.title: Strong duality for flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: A feasible flux balance problem attains its optimum.
nodes.title: Feasible flux balance problem attains its optimum

nodes.summary: There are finitely many affine functions `b ↦ y ⬝ᵥ b + κ` whose minimum is the optimal value at every feasible right-hand side `b`.
nodes.title: The FBA value is piecewise linear

nodes.summary: There is a finite set `T` of pairs `(y, u ⬝ᵥ α - l ⬝ᵥ β)` with `(y, α, β)` dual feasible, such that for every feasible `b` some pair in `T` is optimal: `y ⬝ᵥ b + κ = fbaValue S l u c b`.
nodes.title: Finitely many dual solutions suffice

nodes.summary: If `s₀` is a steady state at enzyme levels `e₀`, the rate laws are continuously differentiable at `s₀`, and the Jacobian `δ ↦ N (e₀ ⊙ f'(s₀) δ)` is injective, then the steady state continues to a map `σ` with `σ e₀ = s₀` satisfying `IsRegularSteadyState`.
nodes.title: Regular steady states exist by the implicit function theorem

nodes.summary: Shadow prices (Orth, Thiele & Palsson 2010): at a feasible `b`, the metabolite prices `y` of the optimal dual solutions are exactly the supergradients of the optimal value: `fbaValue b' ≤ fbaValue b + y ⬝ᵥ (b' - b)` for every feasible `b'`.
nodes.title: Shadow prices

nodes.summary: Symmetric matrix balancing (Sinkhorn 1964; the "equal visibility" normalization of Imakaev et al. 2012): a symmetric matrix with positive entries has a unique positive vector `d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic.
nodes.title: Symmetric matrix balancing

nodes.summary: Dual feasibility for flux balance analysis: `y` prices the metabolites, `α, β ≥ 0` the upper and lower flux bounds, and `Sᵀ y + α - β = c`.
nodes.title: Dual feasibility for flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: The dual objective `b ⬝ᵥ y + u ⬝ᵥ α - l ⬝ᵥ β`.
nodes.title: Dual objective of flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: The feasible fluxes of flux balance analysis: `S v = b`, `l ≤ v ≤ u`.
nodes.title: Feasible fluxes of flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: The optimal value is concave in the right-hand side `b` on the set of feasible `b`.
nodes.title: Concavity of the flux balance optimum in the right-hand side

nodes.summary: The optimal value `max {c ⬝ᵥ v | S v = b, l ≤ v ≤ u}` of flux balance analysis (the supremum; it is `0` by convention when the problem is infeasible).
nodes.title: Optimal value of flux balance analysis

nodes.summary: The state reached from `x` by one firing of reaction `r`, `x - src r + prod r` (meaningful when `src r ≤ x`, the only case in which the propensity is nonzero).
nodes.title: State after one reaction firing

nodes.summary: The flux control coefficient `C^{J_j}_{e_i} = (e_i / J_j) ∂J_j/∂e_i`. It is meaningful when `J_j ≠ 0` and the steady-state flux is differentiable at `e`; otherwise Lean's `x / 0 = 0` and `fderiv` of a non-differentiable map, `0`, give junk values.
nodes.title: Flux control coefficient

nodes.summary: Reaction rates `v_i(e, s) = e_i f_i(s)` proportional to enzyme levels `e`.
nodes.title: Reaction fluxes proportional to enzyme levels

nodes.summary: If `b` is an interior point of the set of feasible right-hand sides and `y` is the only metabolite price vector of an optimal dual solution, then the optimal value is differentiable at `b` with derivative `b' ↦ y ⬝ᵥ b'`.
nodes.title: Shadow prices are derivatives when unique

nodes.summary: Necessity of total support (Sinkhorn & Knopp 1967; Csima & Datta 1972): if a positive diagonal scaling `diag(d) A diag(d)` is doubly stochastic, then `A` has total support. The proof uses Birkhoff's theorem. The converse for symmetric nonnegative `A` is `exists_symmetric_balancing_of_hasTotalSupport`.
nodes.title: Necessity of total support

nodes.summary: A square matrix has total support if it is nonzero and every positive entry lies on a positive diagonal: for `A i j > 0` there is a permutation `σ` with `σ i = j` and `A k (σ k) > 0` for all `k` (Sinkhorn & Knopp 1967; Csima & Datta 1972).
nodes.title: Total support of a square matrix

nodes.summary: In the interaction graph of `f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1}ⁿ` there is an edge `j → i` when the `i`-th coordinate of `f` depends on the `j`-th variable.
nodes.title: Interaction graph of a Boolean network

nodes.summary: The interaction graph of `f` has no directed cycle (loops included).
nodes.title: Acyclic interaction graph

nodes.summary: `t : ι → ι` is a spanning in-tree rooted at `r` (each `i ≠ r` points to its parent `t i`): `t r = r` and iterating `t` from any state reaches `r`.
nodes.title: Spanning in-tree rooted at a state

nodes.summary: A rate matrix is irreducible if every state reaches every other state through positive jump rates.
nodes.title: Irreducible rate matrix

nodes.summary: The restricted generator is a rate matrix when the rate constants are nonnegative and `Ω` is closed under the reactions.
nodes.title: Restricted mass-action generator is a rate matrix

nodes.summary: A regular steady state at enzyme levels `e₀`: `σ` is differentiable at `e₀`, the rate laws are differentiable at `σ e₀`, `N v(e, σ e) = 0` for `e` near `e₀`, and the Jacobian `δ ↦ N ∂_s v(e₀, σ e₀) δ` is injective (it is square, so this is its invertibility).
nodes.title: Regular steady state of a metabolic network

nodes.summary: Global balance of the product-form Poisson weights (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1): if `c` is complex balanced for the deterministic mass-action system with rate constants `k`, then at every state `x` the total outflow `π(x) ∑_r λ_r(x)` equals the total inflow `∑_{r : prod r ≤ x} π(x - prod r + src r) λ_r(x - prod r + src r)` for `π = poissonWeight c`. This is an algebraic identity valid for all real `k`…
nodes.title: Global balance of the product-form Poisson weights

nodes.summary: Anderson–Craciun–Kurtz on a finite class (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1–4.2): if `c` is complex balanced and every state of `Ω` from which a reaction leads into `Ω` lies in `Ω` (`hbwd`), the Poisson weights restricted to `Ω` are invariant for the restricted generator: `π Q = 0`, for all real `k` and `c`. For a closed communicating class of a weakly reversible network with positive rate constants `hbwd`…
nodes.title: Anderson–Craciun–Kurtz on a finite class

nodes.summary: The product-form Poisson weight `∏_s c_s ^ x_s e^{-c_s} / Nat.factorial x_s` of a state `x`.
nodes.title: Product-form Poisson weight of a state

nodes.summary: The stochastic mass-action propensity of reaction `r` in state `x` (molecule counts): `k r * ∏_s x_s (x_s - 1) ⋯ (x_s - src_s + 1)`, the falling factorial `Nat.descFactorial x_s src_s` (it vanishes when `x_s < src_s`). Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz (2010), §2.
nodes.title: Stochastic mass-action propensity

nodes.summary: Robert's theorem (Robert 1980): if the interaction graph of `f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1}ⁿ` is acyclic, `f` has a unique fixed point `p`, and every synchronous trajectory reaches it within `n` steps.
nodes.title: Robert's theorem

nodes.summary: Two diagonal scalings of a positive matrix to doubly stochastic form differ by a positive scalar.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of Sinkhorn scaling

nodes.summary: The steady-state fluxes `J(e) = v(e, σ(e))` along a steady-state map `σ`.
nodes.title: Steady-state fluxes along a steady-state map

nodes.summary: Concentration summation theorem (Heinrich & Rapoport 1974): for a positive steady-state concentration `s_m`, `∑_i C^{s_m}_{e_i} = 0`. The positivity hypothesis is the domain on which the scaled concentration control coefficients have their biological meaning.
nodes.title: Concentration summation theorem

nodes.summary: Flux connectivity theorem (Kacser & Burns 1973): when all steady-state fluxes are nonzero, `∑_i C^{J_j}_{e_i} ε^{v_i}_{s_m} = 0` for every flux `J_j` and metabolite `s_m`.
nodes.title: Flux connectivity theorem

nodes.summary: Flux summation theorem (Kacser & Burns 1973; Heinrich & Rapoport 1974): for a nonzero steady-state flux `J_j`, `∑_i C^{J_j}_{e_i} = 1`.
nodes.title: Flux summation theorem

nodes.summary: For an irreducible rate matrix every in-tree weight is positive.
nodes.title: In-tree weights of an irreducible rate matrix are positive

nodes.summary: Markov chain tree theorem (King & Altman 1956; Hill 1966): the in-tree weights are invariant for every matrix with zero row sums, `w Q = 0`. The proof matches both sides with the maps `g : ι → ι` whose functional graph has its cycle through `j` (Anantharam & Tsoucas 1989).
nodes.title: Markov chain tree theorem

nodes.summary: The total weight `∑_t ∏_{i ≠ r} Q i (t i)` of the spanning in-trees rooted at `r`.
nodes.title: Total weight of spanning in-trees

nodes.summary: The state from which one firing of reaction `r` leads to `x`, `x - prod r + src r` (meaningful when `prod r ≤ x`).
nodes.title: State before one reaction firing
